findings.reason: the honest change is to extend the owner at reckon/capabilities.py by parameterizing it with the override env-var name and sub-directory, so both caches resolve through one resolver rather than a fork that can diverge.
findings.text: _profile_cache_root() re-implements the four-step cache-root precedence already owned by capabilities.pick_input_cache_root() at reckon/capabilities.py:1143 (env override, then RECKON_HOME/cache, then XDG_CACHE_HOME/reckon, then ~/.cache/reckon), copying its "RECKON_HOME must outrank XDG_CACHE_HOME or a test writes the live cache" rationale into both docstrings, so a plan whose sections 6 and 8 nodes add two cross-process stores now resolves their roots through two parallel copies that can drift

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one public function hides substantial behaviour: pick(request, config) -> Selection (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:47) hides the ledger read, the budget view, candidate eligibility, the prompt render, the Jev call, its validation and the fallback; the sub-modules (snapshot=eligibility, lane_context=state, outcomes=reporting) sit on distinct concerns, not repeated wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the picker forked the fleet's shared cache-root resolution into a second resolver rather than extending reckon/capabilities.py, whose owner file is named below.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase before adding the picker: its picker-reuse-map node mapped 28 base-revision functions, snapshot.py is documented as adapting the existing gates and measurements, and the code imports and reuses the owners it names (routing._competence_verdict, capability.assess_execution_fit, budget.policy, lane_document.read_lane_document, dispatch._lane_worker_allowance, flight._probe_serving, resumption._read_lane_probe_cache — reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:150-190).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the picker is a judgment layer, not a re-implementation: code keeps every hard constraint (snapshot.py reuses the routing/dispatch/budget gates) and Jev supplies only the pressure judgment the deterministic gates lack (sections 4 and 10), which is the justification the item asks for. The plan's separate consolidation — "one lane per provider", section 1 row 3, deferred by section 5's landed summary to section 11 — is not a wrapper defect, but section 11 landed as the model catalogue and carries no consolidation record, so the plan's headline premise has no landing and should be restated or re-scoped.
